GV.OC-01.title: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
GV.OC-01.description: The organization's mission, stakeholder expectations, legal and regulatory requirements, and cybersecurity risk strategy are defined and communicated.

GV.OC-02.title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood and cybersecurity risk communicated
GV.OC-02.description: Stakeholders with interest in cybersecurity risk outcomes are identified, their needs are understood, and risk information is communicated.

GV.OC-03.title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity are understood
GV.OC-03.description: The organization understands applicable cybersecurity-related laws, regulations, and contractual requirements.

GV.RM-01.title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
GV.RM-01.description: Risk tolerance and appetite, along with cybersecurity risk management strategy, are established and agreed upon.

GV.RM-02.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
GV.RM-02.description: The organization's risk appetite and risk tolerance are established, documented, and inform risk management decisions.

GV.RM-03.title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management
GV.RM-03.description: Cybersecurity risk management is integrated into enterprise-wide risk management processes.

GV.RR-01.title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk
GV.RR-01.description: Senior leadership understands their responsibility for cybersecurity risk and champions cybersecurity risk management.

GV.RR-02.title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established
GV.RR-02.description: Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities for all relevant personnel are defined and communicated.

GV.PO-01.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established, communicated, and enforced
GV.PO-01.description: Cybersecurity policy is established based on organizational mission, strategy, risk appetite, and legal requirements.

GV.PO-02.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced
GV.PO-02.description: The cybersecurity policy is regularly reviewed and updated to reflect changes in risk, technology, and legal requirements.

ID.AM-01.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
ID.AM-01.description: Physical devices and systems within the organization are inventoried and managed.

ID.AM-02.title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
ID.AM-02.description: Software platforms and applications within the organization are inventoried.

ID.AM-03.title: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
ID.AM-03.description: Network data flows are documented and maintained.

ID.AM-07.title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
ID.AM-07.description: Data assets and their metadata are inventoried and managed throughout their lifecycle.

ID.RA-01.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
ID.RA-01.description: Vulnerabilities in organizational assets are identified, assessed, and documented to support risk mitigation.

ID.RA-02.title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
ID.RA-02.description: Threat intelligence is gathered, analyzed, and used to inform risk decisions.

ID.RA-05.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
ID.RA-05.description: Risk assessments combine threat, vulnerability, likelihood, and impact information to prioritize responses.

ID.RA-06.title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
ID.RA-06.description: Risk responses including mitigation, transfer, acceptance, or avoidance are selected and tracked.

PR.AA-01.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed
PR.AA-01.description: User accounts, service credentials, and device identities are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited.

PR.AA-02.title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on appropriate context
PR.AA-02.description: Identity proofing establishes trust in user identities before credentials are issued.

PR.AA-03.title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
PR.AA-03.description: Authentication mechanisms are used to verify the identity of users, services, and devices before access is granted.

PR.AA-04.title: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
PR.AA-04.description: Identity assertion mechanisms such as tokens and certificates are protected against forgery and replay attacks.

PR.AA-05.title: Access to assets is granted to authorized users, services, and hardware
PR.AA-05.description: Access control policies enforce least privilege, need-to-know, and separation of duties.

PR.AA-06.title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
PR.AA-06.description: Physical access controls protect assets from unauthorized physical access.

PR.AT-01.title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks
PR.AT-01.description: All personnel receive cybersecurity awareness training appropriate to their role.

PR.DS-01.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
PR.DS-01.description: Data stored in databases, files, and backup media is protected using encryption and access control.

PR.DS-02.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
PR.DS-02.description: Data transmitted over networks is protected using encryption and integrity controls.

PR.DS-10.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
PR.DS-10.description: Data being processed is protected against unauthorized access and manipulation.

PR.DS-11.title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested
PR.DS-11.description: Data backup procedures are in place and tested regularly to ensure data availability.

PR.IR-01.title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
PR.IR-01.description: Network segmentation, firewalls, and other controls protect the network from unauthorized access.

PR.IR-02.title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats
PR.IR-02.description: Physical and environmental controls protect technology assets from threats like fire, flood, and power failure.

PR.PS-01.title: Configuration management practices are established and applied
PR.PS-01.description: Secure configuration baselines are established for all technology assets and enforced.

PR.PS-02.title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
PR.PS-02.description: Software patching, updating, and removal processes are in place to manage risk from outdated software.

PR.PS-03.title: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
PR.PS-03.description: Hardware lifecycle management including patching firmware and replacing end-of-life hardware.

PR.PS-04.title: Log records are generated to enable monitoring, forensics, and incident response activities
PR.PS-04.description: Logging is configured appropriately on all systems to support security monitoring and forensics.

PR.PS-05.title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
PR.PS-05.description: Application allowlisting and software execution controls prevent unauthorized software from running.

PR.PS-06.title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their security is evaluated
PR.PS-06.description: Secure SDLC practices including code review, SAST, DAST, and security testing are integrated.

DE.AE-02.title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better characterize them and detect cybersecurity incidents
DE.AE-02.description: Anomalous activity and events are analyzed to identify potential cybersecurity incidents.

DE.AE-03.title: Event data are aggregated and correlated from multiple sources and sensors
DE.AE-03.description: Security events from multiple sources are correlated to identify attack patterns.

DE.AE-06.title: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
DE.AE-06.description: Security event information is shared with appropriate personnel and automated tools for response.

DE.CM-01.title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
DE.CM-01.description: Network traffic is monitored continuously for signs of malicious activity.

DE.CM-03.title: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
DE.CM-03.description: User behavior and system access are monitored to detect insider threats and misuse.

DE.CM-06.title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
DE.CM-06.description: Third-party and external service provider activities are monitored for security issues.

DE.CM-09.title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored
DE.CM-09.description: System resources including CPU, memory, and processes are monitored for anomalies.

RS.MA-01.title: The response to a detected cybersecurity incident is managed
RS.MA-01.description: Incidents are assigned to responsible personnel and managed through to resolution.

RS.MA-02.title: Incidents are prioritized and selected based on response strategies and objectives
RS.MA-02.description: Incidents are triaged and prioritized based on severity, impact, and business context.

RS.MA-03.title: Incidents are categorized and classified based on response strategies
RS.MA-03.description: Incident classification guides the selection of appropriate response procedures.

RS.AN-03.title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident
RS.AN-03.description: Root cause analysis is conducted for security incidents to understand how they occurred.

RS.AN-06.title: Actions taken during an investigation are recorded
RS.AN-06.description: Investigation actions are logged and maintained for evidence and audit purposes.

RS.MI-01.title: Incidents are contained
RS.MI-01.description: Containment actions are taken to limit the spread and impact of security incidents.

RS.MI-02.title: Incidents are eradicated
RS.MI-02.description: The root cause of incidents is eliminated and affected systems are remediated.

RC.RP-01.title: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
RC.RP-01.description: Recovery procedures are executed to restore systems and services to normal operation.

RC.RP-02.title: Recovery tasks are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
RC.RP-02.description: Recovery activities are planned, prioritized, and tracked to completion.

RC.RP-04.title: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them in recovery
RC.RP-04.description: Backup integrity is verified using checksums and testing before use in recovery.

RC.CO-03.title: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated stakeholders
RC.CO-03.description: Recovery progress is communicated to stakeholders throughout the recovery process.

CIS-1.title: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets
CIS-1.description: Actively manage (inventory, track, and correct) all enterprise assets connected to the infrastructure physically, virtually, remotely, and those within cloud environments to know the totality of assets that need to be monitored and protected.

CIS-1.1.title: Establish and Maintain Detailed Enterprise Asset Inventory
CIS-1.1.description: Establish and maintain an accurate, detailed, and up-to-date inventory of all enterprise assets with potential to store, process or transmit data.

CIS-2.title: Inventory and Control of Software Assets
CIS-2.description: Actively manage (inventory, track, and correct) all software on the network so that only authorized software is installed and can execute, and that unauthorized and unmanaged software is found and prevented from installation or execution.

CIS-2.2.title: Ensure Authorized Software is Currently Supported
CIS-2.2.description: Ensure that only currently supported software is designated as authorized in the software inventory for enterprise assets.

CIS-3.title: Data Protection
CIS-3.description: Develop processes and technical controls to identify, classify, securely handle, retain, and dispose of data.

CIS-3.3.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
CIS-3.3.description: Configure data access control lists based on a user's need to know. Apply data access control lists, also known as access permissions, to local and remote file systems, databases, and applications.

CIS-3.6.title: Encrypt Data on End-User Devices
CIS-3.6.description: Encrypt data on end-user devices containing sensitive data.

CIS-3.10.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data in Transit
CIS-3.10.description: Encrypt sensitive data in transit using only authenticated protocols with at least TLS 1.2.

CIS-3.11.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data at Rest
CIS-3.11.description: Encrypt sensitive data at rest on servers, applications, and databases containing sensitive data.

CIS-4.title: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software
CIS-4.description: Establish and maintain the secure configuration of enterprise assets and software.

CIS-4.1.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process
CIS-4.1.description: Establish and maintain a secure configuration process for enterprise assets and software.

CIS-4.2.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process for Network Infrastructure
CIS-4.2.description: Establish and maintain a secure configuration process for network devices.

CIS-4.8.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
CIS-4.8.description: Uninstall or disable unnecessary services on enterprise assets and software, such as an unused file sharing service, web application module, or service function.

CIS-5.title: Account Management
CIS-5.description: Use processes and tools to assign and manage authorization to credentials for user accounts including administrator accounts as well as service and application accounts.

CIS-5.2.title: Use Unique Passwords
CIS-5.2.description: Use unique passwords for all enterprise assets. Best practice implementation includes, at minimum, an 8-character password for accounts using MFA and a 14-character password for accounts not using MFA.

CIS-5.4.title: Restrict Administrator Privileges to Dedicated Administrator Accounts
CIS-5.4.description: Restrict administrator privileges to dedicated administrator accounts on enterprise assets.

CIS-6.title: Access Control Management
CIS-6.description: Use processes and tools to create, assign, manage, and revoke access credentials and privileges for user, administrator, and service/application accounts.

CIS-6.3.title: Require MFA for Externally-Exposed Applications
CIS-6.3.description: Require all externally-exposed enterprise or third-party applications to enforce MFA, where supported.

CIS-6.5.title: Require MFA for Administrative Access
CIS-6.5.description: Require MFA for all administrative access accounts.

CIS-6.8.title: Define and Maintain Role-Based Access Control
CIS-6.8.description: Define and maintain role-based access control, through determining and documenting the access rights necessary for each role within the enterprise to successfully carry out its assigned duties.

CIS-7.title: Continuous Vulnerability Management
CIS-7.description: Develop a plan to continuously assess and track vulnerabilities on all enterprise assets within the enterprise's infrastructure, in order to remediate, and minimize, the window of opportunity for attackers.

CIS-7.3.title: Perform Automated Operating System Patch Management
CIS-7.3.description: Perform operating system updates on enterprise assets through automated patch management on a monthly, or more frequent, basis.

CIS-7.4.title: Perform Automated Application Patch Management
CIS-7.4.description: Perform application updates on enterprise assets through automated patch management on a monthly, or more frequent, basis.

CIS-8.title: Audit Log Management
CIS-8.description: Collect, alert, review, and retain audit logs of events that could help detect, understand, or recover from an attack.

CIS-8.2.title: Collect Audit Logs
CIS-8.2.description: Collect audit logs. Ensure that logging is enabled across enterprise assets.

CIS-8.5.title: Collect Detailed Audit Logs
CIS-8.5.description: Configure detailed audit logging for enterprise assets containing sensitive data. Include event source, date, username, timestamp, source addresses, destination addresses, and other useful elements.

CIS-9.title: Email and Web Browser Protections
CIS-9.description: Improve protections and detections of threats from email and web vectors, as these are opportunities for attackers to manipulate human behavior through direct engagement.

CIS-10.title: Malware Defenses
CIS-10.description: Prevent or control the installation, spread, and execution of malicious applications, code, or scripts on enterprise assets.

CIS-11.title: Data Recovery
CIS-11.description: Establish and maintain data recovery practices sufficient to restore in-scope enterprise assets to a pre-incident and trusted state.

CIS-12.title: Network Infrastructure Management
CIS-12.description: Establish, implement, and actively manage network devices in order to prevent attackers from exploiting vulnerable network services and access points.

CIS-13.title: Network Monitoring and Defense
CIS-13.description: Operate processes and tooling to establish and maintain comprehensive network monitoring and defense against security threats.

CIS-14.title: Security Awareness and Skills Training
CIS-14.description: Establish and maintain a security awareness program to influence behavior among the workforce to be security conscious and properly skilled to reduce cybersecurity risks.

CIS-15.title: Service Provider Management
CIS-15.description: Develop a process to evaluate service providers who hold sensitive data or are responsible for an enterprise's critical IT platforms or processes.

CIS-16.title: Application Software Security
CIS-16.description: Manage the security life cycle of in-house developed, hosted, or acquired software in order to prevent, detect, and remediate security weaknesses before they can impact the enterprise.

CIS-16.1.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Application Development Process
CIS-16.1.description: Establish and maintain a secure application development process. In the process, address such items as secure application design standards, secure coding practices, developer training, and secure code reviews.

CIS-16.2.title: Establish and Maintain a Process to Accept and Address Software Vulnerabilities
CIS-16.2.description: Establish and maintain a process to accept and address reports of software vulnerabilities, including providing a means for external entities to report.

CIS-16.4.title: Establish and Manage an Inventory of Third-Party Software Components
CIS-16.4.description: Establish and manage an updated inventory of third-party components used in development, often referred to as a Bill of Materials.

CIS-16.6.title: Establish and Maintain a Severity Rating System and Process for Application Vulnerabilities
CIS-16.6.description: Establish and maintain a severity rating system and process for application vulnerabilities that facilitates prioritizing the order in which discovered vulnerabilities are fixed.

CIS-16.7.title: Use Standard Hardening Configuration Templates for Application Infrastructure
CIS-16.7.description: Use standard, industry-recommended hardening configuration templates for application infrastructure components.

CIS-16.9.title: Train Developers in Application Security Concepts and Secure Coding
CIS-16.9.description: Ensure that all software development personnel receive training in writing secure code for their specific development environment and responsibilities.

CIS-16.12.title: Implement Code-Level Security Checks
CIS-16.12.description: Apply static code analysis tools to verify that coding practices meet defined security standards.

CIS-17.title: Incident Response Management
CIS-17.description: Establish a program to develop and maintain an incident response capability in order to prepare, detect, and quickly respond to an attack.

CIS-18.title: Penetration Testing
CIS-18.description: Test the effectiveness and resiliency of enterprise assets through identifying and exploiting weaknesses in controls and simulating the objectives and actions of an attacker.

CIS-18.2.title: Perform Periodic External Penetration Tests
CIS-18.2.description: Perform periodic external penetration tests based on program requirements, no less than annually.

CIS-18.3.title: Remediate Penetration Test Findings
CIS-18.3.description: Remediate penetration test findings based on the enterprise's policy for remediation scope and prioritization.

ASVS-V1.1.title: Secure Software Development Lifecycle
ASVS-V1.1.description: Verify the use of a secure software development lifecycle that addresses security in all phases of development. Security requirements must be defined and reviewed. Threat modelling must be performed for new features.

ASVS-V1.2.title: Authentication Architecture
ASVS-V1.2.description: Verify that all application components use a single, vetted, and tested authentication mechanism. Authentication must use strong server-side controls.

ASVS-V1.4.title: Access Control Architecture
ASVS-V1.4.description: Verify that trusted enforcement points such as access control gateways, servers, and serverless functions enforce access controls. Do not enforce access controls on the client.

ASVS-V2.1.title: Password Security
ASVS-V2.1.description: Verify that user set passwords are at least 12 characters in length, allow spaces and special characters, and that there is no upper limit on password length. Passwords must not be stored using reversible or weak hashing algorithms.

ASVS-V2.2.title: General Authenticator Security
ASVS-V2.2.description: Verify that anti-automation controls are effective at mitigating breached credential testing, brute force, and account lockout attacks. Verify that credential hints are not used.

ASVS-V2.3.title: Authenticator Lifecycle
ASVS-V2.3.description: Verify that the system can detect and alert on authentication anomalies such as by country, by device, and recently used IP addresses.

ASVS-V2.4.title: Credential Storage
ASVS-V2.4.description: Verify that passwords are stored using an approved adaptive one-way hashing algorithm with a work factor of at least 600,000 iterations for PBKDF2, or using bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2id with appropriate cost factors.

ASVS-V2.7.title: Out of Band Verification
ASVS-V2.7.description: Verify that out of band verifier generated OTPs or other codes have sufficient randomness, expire after a short period, are single-use only, and transmitted via a secure channel.

ASVS-V2.8.title: Single or Multi Factor One Time Verifier
ASVS-V2.8.description: Verify that time-based OTPs have a defined lifetime before expiring. One-time authentication codes must be invalidated after use.

ASVS-V3.1.title: Fundamental Session Management Security
ASVS-V3.1.description: Verify that the application never reveals session tokens in URL parameters or error messages. Session tokens must be stored securely and never transmitted in plaintext.

ASVS-V3.2.title: Session Binding
ASVS-V3.2.description: Verify the application generates a new session token on user authentication. Session tokens must have at least 64 bits of entropy and be stored securely.

ASVS-V3.3.title: Session Timeout
ASVS-V3.3.description: Verify that logout and expiration invalidate the session token. Sessions should expire after a defined period of inactivity.

ASVS-V3.4.title: Cookie-based Session Management
ASVS-V3.4.description: Verify that cookie-based session tokens have the Secure attribute set, use the HttpOnly attribute, and use the SameSite attribute to limit exposure to cross-site request forgery attacks.

ASVS-V4.1.title: General Access Control Design
ASVS-V4.1.description: Verify that the principle of least privilege exists – users should only be able to access functions, data files, URLs, controllers, services, and other resources for which they have specific authorisation.

ASVS-V4.2.title: Operation Level Access Control
ASVS-V4.2.description: Verify that sensitive data and APIs are protected against Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) attacks targeting creation, reading, updating, and deletion of records.

ASVS-V5.1.title: Input Validation
ASVS-V5.1.description: Verify that the application has defenses against HTTP parameter pollution attacks. Verify that all input is validated using positive validation (allow lists), not negative validation (deny lists or sanitization).

ASVS-V5.2.title: Sanitization and Sandboxing
ASVS-V5.2.description: Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar is properly sanitized with an HTML sanitizer library or framework feature.

ASVS-V5.3.title: Output Encoding and Injection Prevention
ASVS-V5.3.description: Verify that output encoding is relevant for the interpreter and context required. All injection attacks must be prevented including SQL injection, command injection, LDAP injection, XPath injection, and XSS.

ASVS-V5.4.title: Memory, String and Unmanaged Code
ASVS-V5.4.description: Verify that the application uses memory-safe string, safer memory copy and pointer arithmetic to detect or prevent stack, buffer, or heap overflows.

ASVS-V5.5.title: Deserialization Prevention
ASVS-V5.5.description: Verify that serialized objects use integrity checks or are encrypted to prevent hostile object creation or data tampering.

ASVS-V6.1.title: Data Classification
ASVS-V6.1.description: Verify that regulated private data is stored encrypted while at rest, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII), sensitive personal information, or data assessed likely to be subject to EU's GDPR.

ASVS-V6.2.title: Algorithms
ASVS-V6.2.description: Verify that all cryptographic modules fail securely, and errors are handled in a way that does not enable Padding Oracle attacks. Weak algorithms such as MD5, SHA1, DES, RC4, and RSA-1024 must not be used.

ASVS-V6.3.title: Random Values
ASVS-V6.3.description: Verify that all random numbers, random file names, random GUIDs, and random strings are generated using the cryptographic module's approved cryptographically secure random number generator.

ASVS-V6.4.title: Secret Management
ASVS-V6.4.description: Verify that secrets, API keys, and passwords are not included in source code, or online source code repositories. Secrets must be stored in a vault or encrypted configuration.

ASVS-V7.1.title: Log Content
ASVS-V7.1.description: Verify that the application does not log credentials or payment details. Verify that sensitive information is not logged.

ASVS-V7.2.title: Log Processing
ASVS-V7.2.description: Verify that all authentication decisions are logged, with sufficient user context to identify suspicious or malicious accounts.

ASVS-V7.4.title: Error Handling
ASVS-V7.4.description: Verify that a generic message is shown when an unexpected or security sensitive error occurs, potentially with a unique ID which support personnel can use to investigate.

ASVS-V8.1.title: General Data Protection
ASVS-V8.1.description: Verify that the application protects sensitive data from being cached in server components such as load balancers and application caches.

ASVS-V8.2.title: Client-side Data Protection
ASVS-V8.2.description: Verify that sensitive data is not stored in browser storage (localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB), cookie stores, or Flash cookie stores.

ASVS-V8.3.title: Sensitive Private Data
ASVS-V8.3.description: Verify that sensitive data is transmitted to the server in the HTTP message body or headers, and that query string parameters from any HTTP verb do not contain sensitive data.

ASVS-V9.1.title: Client Communication Security
ASVS-V9.1.description: Verify that TLS is used for all client connectivity, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications. The application must use TLS 1.2 or higher.

ASVS-V9.2.title: Server Communication Security
ASVS-V9.2.description: Verify that connections to and from the server use trusted TLS certificates. The application must validate TLS certificates before using them.

ASVS-V10.1.title: Code Integrity Controls
ASVS-V10.1.description: Verify that a code analysis tool is in use that can detect potentially malicious code, such as time functions, unsafe file operations, or network connections.

ASVS-V10.2.title: Malicious Code Search
ASVS-V10.2.description: Verify that the application source code and third party libraries do not contain back doors, Easter eggs, and logic bombs.

ASVS-V10.3.title: Deployed Application Integrity Controls
ASVS-V10.3.description: Verify that if the application has a client or server auto-update feature, updates should be obtained over secure channels and digitally signed.

ASVS-V11.1.title: Business Logic Security
ASVS-V11.1.description: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in sequential step order and without skipping steps.

ASVS-V12.1.title: File Upload
ASVS-V12.1.description: Verify that the application will not accept large files that could fill up storage or cause a denial of service.

ASVS-V12.3.title: File Execution Prevention
ASVS-V12.3.description: Verify that user-submitted filename metadata is not used directly by system or framework filesystems and that a URL API is used to protect against path traversal.

ASVS-V12.4.title: File Storage
ASVS-V12.4.description: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are validated to be of expected type and are not accessible directly as user-supplied content.

ASVS-V13.1.title: Generic Web Service Security
ASVS-V13.1.description: Verify that all application components use the same encodings and parsers to avoid parsing attacks that exploit different URI or file parsing behavior that could be used in SSRF and RFI attacks.

ASVS-V13.2.title: RESTful Web Service
ASVS-V13.2.description: Verify that RESTful web services that utilize cookies are protected from Cross-Site Request Forgery via the use of at least one or more of: triple or double submit cookie pattern, CSRF nonces, or ORIGIN request header checks.

ASVS-V13.3.title: SOAP Web Service
ASVS-V13.3.description: Verify that XSD schema validation takes place to ensure a properly formed XML document, followed by validation of each input field before any processing of that data takes place.

ASVS-V13.4.title: GraphQL
ASVS-V13.4.description: Verify that GraphQL or other data layer authorization logic should be implemented at the business logic layer instead of the GraphQL layer.

ASVS-V14.1.title: Build and Deploy
ASVS-V14.1.description: Verify that build pipelines warn about out-of-date or insecure components and that appropriate action is taken. Verify that the build pipeline performs automated security testing including SAST and SCA.

ASVS-V14.2.title: Dependency
ASVS-V14.2.description: Verify that all third-party components used by the application are from expected repositories, and that known vulnerable third-party libraries are not used.

ASVS-V14.3.title: Unintended Security Disclosure
ASVS-V14.3.description: Verify that web or application server and application framework debug modes are disabled in production to eliminate debug features, developer consoles, and unintended security disclosures.

ASVS-V14.4.title: HTTP Security Headers
ASVS-V14.4.description: Verify that every HTTP response contains a Content-Type header. Verify that security headers including X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, Content-Security-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security are set appropriately.

ASVS-V14.5.title: HTTP Request Header Validation
ASVS-V14.5.description: Verify that the application server only accepts the HTTP methods in use by the application and logs or alerts on any requests using methods not intended for use by the application.

A.5.1.title: Policies for information security
A.5.1.description: Information security policies shall be defined, approved by management, published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel and interested parties, and reviewed at planned intervals or if significant changes occur.

A.5.2.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
A.5.2.description: Information security roles and responsibilities shall be defined and allocated according to the organization needs.

A.5.7.title: Threat intelligence
A.5.7.description: Information relating to information security threats shall be collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence.

A.5.8.title: Information security in project management
A.5.8.description: Information security shall be integrated into project management.

A.5.14.title: Information transfer
A.5.14.description: Information transfer rules, procedures, or agreements shall be in place for all types of transfer facilities within the organization and between the organization and other parties.

A.5.15.title: Access control
A.5.15.description: Rules to control physical and logical access to information and other associated assets shall be established and implemented based on business and information security requirements.

A.5.16.title: Identity management
A.5.16.description: The full life cycle of identities shall be managed.

A.5.17.title: Authentication information
A.5.17.description: Allocation and management of authentication information shall be controlled by a management process, including advising personnel on appropriate handling of authentication information.

A.5.20.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
A.5.20.description: Relevant information security requirements shall be established and agreed with each supplier based on the type of supplier relationship.

A.5.23.title: Information security for use of cloud services
A.5.23.description: Processes for acquisition, use, management and exit from cloud services shall be established in accordance with the organization's information security requirements.

A.5.24.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
A.5.24.description: The organization shall plan and prepare for managing information security incidents by defining, establishing and communicating information security incident management processes, roles and responsibilities.

A.5.25.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
A.5.25.description: The organization shall assess information security events and decide if they are to be categorized as information security incidents.

A.5.26.title: Response to information security incidents
A.5.26.description: Information security incidents shall be responded to in accordance with the documented procedures.

A.5.28.title: Collection of evidence
A.5.28.description: The organization shall establish and implement procedures for the identification, collection, acquisition, and preservation of evidence related to information security events.

A.6.1.title: Screening
A.6.1.description: Background verification checks on all candidates shall be carried out prior to joining the organization and on an ongoing basis.

A.6.3.title: Information security awareness, education and training
A.6.3.description: Personnel of the organization and relevant interested parties shall receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training and regular updates of the organization's information security policy.

A.6.8.title: Information security event reporting
A.6.8.description: The organization shall provide a mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected information security events through appropriate channels in a timely manner.

A.7.1.title: Physical security perimeters
A.7.1.description: Security perimeters shall be defined and used to protect areas that contain information and other associated assets.

A.8.2.title: Privileged access rights
A.8.2.description: The allocation and use of privileged access rights shall be restricted and managed.

A.8.3.title: Information access restriction
A.8.3.description: Access to information and other associated assets shall be restricted in accordance with the established topic-specific policy on access control.

A.8.4.title: Access to source code
A.8.4.description: Read and write access to source code, development tools and software libraries shall be appropriately managed.

A.8.5.title: Secure authentication
A.8.5.description: Secure authentication technologies and procedures shall be implemented based on information access restrictions and the topic-specific policy on access control.

A.8.6.title: Capacity management
A.8.6.description: The use of resources shall be monitored and adjusted in line with current and expected capacity requirements.

A.8.7.title: Protection against malware
A.8.7.description: Protection against malware shall be implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness.

A.8.8.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
A.8.8.description: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use shall be obtained in a timely fashion, the organization's exposure to such vulnerabilities evaluated and appropriate measures taken.

A.8.9.title: Configuration management
A.8.9.description: Configurations, including security configurations, of hardware, software, services and networks shall be established, documented, implemented, monitored and reviewed.

A.8.10.title: Information deletion
A.8.10.description: Information stored in information systems, devices or in any other storage media shall be deleted when no longer required.

A.8.11.title: Data masking
A.8.11.description: Data masking shall be used in accordance with the organization's topic-specific policy on access control and other related topic-specific policies, and business requirements.

A.8.12.title: Data leakage prevention
A.8.12.description: Data leakage prevention measures shall be applied to systems, networks and any other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.

A.8.13.title: Information backup
A.8.13.description: Backup copies of information, software and systems shall be maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed topic-specific policy on backup.

A.8.15.title: Logging
A.8.15.description: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events shall be produced, stored, protected and analysed.

A.8.16.title: Monitoring activities
A.8.16.description: Networks, systems and applications shall be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential information security incidents.

A.8.20.title: Networks security
A.8.20.description: Networks and network devices shall be secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.

A.8.21.title: Security of network services
A.8.21.description: Security mechanisms, service levels and service requirements of network services shall be identified, implemented and monitored.

A.8.24.title: Use of cryptography
A.8.24.description: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, shall be defined and implemented.

A.8.25.title: Secure development life cycle
A.8.25.description: Rules for the secure development of software and systems shall be established and applied.

A.8.26.title: Application security requirements
A.8.26.description: Information security requirements shall be identified, specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications.

A.8.27.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
A.8.27.description: Principles for engineering secure systems shall be established, documented, maintained and applied to any information system development activities.

A.8.28.title: Secure coding
A.8.28.description: Secure coding principles shall be applied to software development.

A.8.29.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
A.8.29.description: Security testing processes shall be defined and implemented in the development life cycle.

A.8.30.title: Outsourced development
A.8.30.description: The organization shall direct, monitor and review the activities related to outsourced system development.

A.8.33.title: Test information
A.8.33.description: Test information shall be appropriately selected, protected and managed.

A.8.34.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
A.8.34.description: Audit tests and other assurance activities involving assessment of operational systems shall be planned and agreed between the tester and appropriate management.

ISO27034-ASC-1.title: Security requirements elicitation
ISO27034-ASC-1.description: Security requirements shall be elicited, documented and validated as part of the application development lifecycle. Requirements must cover authentication, authorization, data protection and audit.

ISO27034-ASC-2.title: Threat modelling for applications
ISO27034-ASC-2.description: Threat modelling shall be performed to identify potential attack vectors, threat actors and security controls needed for each application component.

ISO27034-ASC-3.title: Secure application architecture
ISO27034-ASC-3.description: Applications shall be designed using security architecture principles including defence-in-depth, least privilege, fail-safe defaults and complete mediation.

ISO27034-ASC-4.title: Application security control specification
ISO27034-ASC-4.description: All security controls to be implemented in the application shall be specified, including authentication mechanisms, session management, cryptographic controls and input validation.

ISO27034-ASC-5.title: Application authentication mechanisms
ISO27034-ASC-5.description: Applications shall implement secure authentication mechanisms. Weak or broken authentication, hardcoded credentials and session weaknesses are prohibited.

ISO27034-ASC-6.title: Application authorisation and access control
ISO27034-ASC-6.description: Applications shall enforce authorisation decisions to prevent unauthorized access to functions or data. Insecure direct object references, privilege escalation and missing access control checks are prohibited.

ISO27034-ASC-7.title: Session management security
ISO27034-ASC-7.description: Applications shall implement secure session management including secure session identifiers, session expiry, and protection against session hijacking.

ISO27034-ASC-8.title: Input validation
ISO27034-ASC-8.description: All input from untrusted sources shall be validated before processing. Applications shall validate type, length, format and range of all input values.

ISO27034-ASC-9.title: Output encoding and injection prevention
ISO27034-ASC-9.description: Application output shall be encoded appropriately to prevent injection attacks. Cross-site scripting and injection vulnerabilities shall be prevented through proper output encoding.

ISO27034-ASC-10.title: Prevention of injection attacks
ISO27034-ASC-10.description: Applications shall prevent injection vulnerabilities including SQL injection, command injection, LDAP injection and XML injection through parameterised queries and safe API usage.

ISO27034-ASC-11.title: Cryptographic controls in applications
ISO27034-ASC-11.description: Applications shall use approved cryptographic algorithms and key lengths. Weak algorithms (MD5, SHA1, DES, RC4) and hardcoded cryptographic keys shall not be used.

ISO27034-ASC-12.title: Sensitive data protection
ISO27034-ASC-12.description: Applications shall protect sensitive data including PII, credentials, and confidential business data both at rest and in transit. Sensitive data shall not be exposed in logs, URLs or error messages.

ISO27034-ASC-13.title: Transport layer security
ISO27034-ASC-13.description: All communications transmitting sensitive information shall use strong transport layer security (TLS 1.2+). Insecure protocols, invalid certificates and certificate validation failures are prohibited.

ISO27034-ASC-14.title: Secure error handling
ISO27034-ASC-14.description: Applications shall handle errors and exceptions securely. Error messages shall not expose sensitive information, stack traces, or system internals to users.

ISO27034-ASC-15.title: Security event logging
ISO27034-ASC-15.description: Applications shall log security-relevant events including authentication failures, access control failures and input validation failures. Logs shall not contain sensitive data.

ISO27034-ASC-16.title: Secure application configuration
ISO27034-ASC-16.description: Applications shall be deployed with secure configurations. Default credentials, debug modes, and development settings shall be disabled in production.

ISO27034-ASC-17.title: Dependency and component security
ISO27034-ASC-17.description: All third-party libraries, frameworks and components used in applications shall be inventoried and kept up-to-date. Known vulnerable dependencies shall be updated or replaced.

ISO27034-ASC-18.title: Container and infrastructure security
ISO27034-ASC-18.description: Containers, orchestration platforms and infrastructure-as-code shall be configured securely. Containers shall not run as root and shall have resource limits set.

ISO27034-ASC-19.title: Static application security testing (SAST)
ISO27034-ASC-19.description: Static analysis tools shall be used during development to identify security vulnerabilities in source code before deployment.

ISO27034-ASC-20.title: Dynamic application security testing (DAST)
ISO27034-ASC-20.description: Dynamic analysis shall be performed against running applications to identify runtime security vulnerabilities.

ISO27034-ASC-21.title: Security code review
ISO27034-ASC-21.description: Security-focused code reviews shall be conducted for all code changes introducing security-sensitive functionality.

AC-1.title: Policy and Procedures
AC-1.description: Develop, document, and disseminate access control policy addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, and compliance.

AC-2.title: Account Management
AC-2.description: Manage system accounts including identifying account types, establishing conditions for membership, specifying authorized users, requiring approvals, monitoring account usage, and notifying account managers.

AC-3.title: Access Enforcement
AC-3.description: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.

AC-4.title: Information Flow Enforcement
AC-4.description: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on applicable policy.

AC-6.title: Least Privilege
AC-6.description: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users which are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.

AC-7.title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
AC-7.description: Enforce a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts and automatically lock the account when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded.

AC-11.title: Device Lock
AC-11.description: Prevent further access to the system by initiating a session lock after a period of inactivity or upon receiving a request from a user.

AC-17.title: Remote Access
AC-17.description: Establish and document usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed.

AU-2.title: Event Logging
AU-2.description: Identify the types of events that the system is capable of logging in support of the audit function and coordinate the event logging function with other organizations requiring audit-related information.

AU-3.title: Content of Audit Records
AU-3.description: Ensure that audit records contain information that establishes what type of event occurred, when the event occurred, where the event occurred, the source of the event, the outcome of the event, and the identity of individuals associated with the event.

AU-9.title: Protection of Audit Information
AU-9.description: Protect audit information and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.

CA-7.title: Continuous Monitoring
CA-7.description: Develop a system-level continuous monitoring strategy and implement continuous monitoring in accordance with the organization-level continuous monitoring strategy.

CA-8.title: Penetration Testing
CA-8.description: Conduct penetration testing on organizational systems or system components to identify vulnerabilities and weaknesses.

CM-2.title: Baseline Configuration
CM-2.description: Develop, document, and maintain a current baseline configuration of the information system.

CM-6.title: Configuration Settings
CM-6.description: Establish and document configuration settings for technology products employed within the information system that reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements.

CM-7.title: Least Functionality
CM-7.description: Configure the information system to provide only essential capabilities.

CM-8.title: System Component Inventory
CM-8.description: Develop and document an inventory of system components that accurately reflects the current system.

IA-2.title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
IA-2.description: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.

IA-5.title: Authenticator Management
IA-5.description: Manage information system authenticators by verifying the identity of the individual as part of initial authenticator distribution, establishing initial authenticator content, ensuring that authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism, and enforcing administrative procedures.

IA-6.title: Authenticator Feedback
IA-6.description: Obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation by unauthorized individuals.

IA-8.title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users)
IA-8.description: Uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users.

IR-4.title: Incident Handling
IR-4.description: Implement an incident handling capability for security incidents that includes preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery.

IR-5.title: Incident Monitoring
IR-5.description: Track and document information system security incidents.

RA-3.title: Risk Assessment
RA-3.description: Conduct a risk assessment to identify threats and vulnerabilities to organizational operations, organizational assets, and individuals.

RA-5.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
RA-5.description: Monitor and scan for vulnerabilities in the information system and hosted applications and when new vulnerabilities potentially affecting the system are identified and reported.

SC-5.title: Denial of Service Protection
SC-5.description: Implement protections against or limit the effects of denial-of-service attacks.

SC-8.title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
SC-8.description: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and detect changes to information during transmission.

SC-12.title: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
SC-12.description: Establish and manage cryptographic keys when cryptography is employed within the information system.

SC-13.title: Cryptographic Protection
SC-13.description: Implement cryptographic uses and type of cryptography required for each use in accordance with applicable federal laws.

SC-23.title: Session Authenticity
SC-23.description: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.

SC-28.title: Protection of Information at Rest
SC-28.description: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of information at rest.

SI-2.title: Flaw Remediation
SI-2.description: Identify, report, and correct information system flaws; test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects.

SI-3.title: Malicious Code Protection
SI-3.description: Implement malicious code protection mechanisms at information system entry and exit points and at workstations, servers, or mobile computing devices on the network.

SI-10.title: Information Input Validation
SI-10.description: Check the validity of all information input to the information system.

SI-16.title: Memory Protection
SI-16.description: Implement the following controls to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution.

SA-11.title: Developer Testing and Evaluation
SA-11.description: Require the developer of the information system, system component, or information system service to implement a security assessment plan and conduct unit, integration, system, and regression testing.

SA-15.title: Development Process, Standards, and Tools
SA-15.description: Require that the developer uses a documented development process that explicitly addresses security requirements, identifies and resolves security flaws, and documents the results.
